root.claim: A single deterministic fixed-alphabet multitape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: speed up address movement and butterfly arithmetic by recursive linear-network procedures, plug them into Harvey and van der Hoeven's reduction of multiplication to synthetic polynomial transforms, and bound the total cost

motivation.text: Scanning Θ(n) bits at each of Θ(log n) transform levels already costs Θ(n log n), so beating n log n requires power savings in both data movement and arithmetic.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$. We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

children.claim: Address-field interchange costs $O(Vu^\tau)$ and a simultaneous butterfly layer costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with fixed $\tau,\lambda'<1$, where $V$ is the stored bit volume.
children.method: turn a strict rank deficit of two finite linear networks into recursive power savings for both tape procedures

motivation.text: Each procedure reduces a call at parameter mf to s calls at parameter f on volume V/W; since s<Wm the normalized cost grows by less than m per level, which gives a power saving.

quote.quote: This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

children.claim: Arrays of logical volume $V$ stored in lexicographic order admit a toolkit of $O(V)$-time tape operations: digit permutations and moves, splits and merges, cyclic row distribution among $W$ streams, and controlled shifts of a later field.
children.method: collect the linear-time scans that every later procedure is built from

motivation.text: Every later cost bound is a recurrence on time divided by volume, so the primitives must cost O(V) with constants independent of all field lengths; the paper isolates them first so later steps only count calls.

children.claim: Permuting or moving a single radix-$q$ digit, splitting and merging on a digit, and distributing rows cyclically among $W$ streams each cost $O(V)$.

quote.quote: Each of the following operations on an array of volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes:

children.claim: An update $y\mapsto y+a(\text{controls})\bmod q^b$ of a target field that follows its control fields, or multiplication of $y$ by a fixed rational unit, costs $O(V)$.

quote.quote: The next operations are linear because their target field follows their control fields.

children.claim: There are two fixed linear networks, one over $\mathbb F_2$ and one over $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$, each with $W$ wires, that exchange two banks of values, restore all scratch values, and admit nested subspace labels whose edge changes need only $s<Wm$ smaller calls in total.
children.method: build the scalar networks from triple-intersection gather/scatter with scratch restoration, lift them to arrays by frames, and count the residual dimensions of nested subspace labels

motivation.text: The frame identity shows that only endpoint frames determine the array operator, so intermediate frames can be chosen freely to make each edge cheap; nested subspace labels make an edge's cost its dimension change, and the subset construction keeps the total dimension lost small.

quote.quote: Once the scalar routing is fixed, the endpoint frames determine the array operator on each route; the intermediate frames can then be chosen to make each edge change inexpensive.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial scratch values, the eight-row forward schedule changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and restores every scratch wire.

quote.quote: The net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of $a,c$.

children.salient: The net effect does not depend at all on the arbitrary initial contents of the scratch wires.

children.claim: Gather/scatter through central wires gives coefficients depending on $|S\cap T|$, side wires cancel the unwanted ones so each invocation is $y\gets y+x$, and three stages give $(X,Y)\mapsto(-Y,X)$.

quote.quote: Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.salient: Three additive stages compose to an exact signed exchange of banks, which in the bit case is a pure permutation.

children.claim: With an invertible frame $D_v$ at every source, gate and sink, the network on arrays implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, so each route applies only its endpoint frames.

quote.quote: Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.salient: All intermediate frames cancel: only the source and sink frames of each route matter.

children.claim: Gates and terminals receive nondegenerate subspaces of an $m$-dimensional bilinear space, nested along every edge, with the only decreasing edges being the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4.

quote.quote: Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels.

children.claim: The total dimension lost on decreasing edges satisfies $L/N<1/2$ in both networks, which leaves a strict deficit $s<Wm$.

quote.quote: In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.salient: The relative deficit $1-s/(Wm)$ is minute (about $10^{-11}$) yet strictly positive, and it alone produces the power saving.

adds.name: wire count
adds.meaning: The number of wires (roles) of the network, including scratch wires.

adds.name: label dimension
adds.meaning: The dimension $m=100^3$ of the bilinear label space.

adds.name: smaller-call count
adds.meaning: The total number of smaller calls needed over all edges of the network.

children.claim: Since $s/W<m^\tau$ with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$, a call at parameter $mf$ done by $s$ calls at parameter $f$ on volume $V/W$ gives normalized cost $O(f^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$.

children.salient: Each level multiplies the parameter by $m$ but the normalized cost by less than $m$, so the exponent drops strictly below one.

children.claim: Two disjoint contiguous $u$-bit address fields of an array of volume $V$ can be interchanged in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time.
children.method: implement each edge's matrix shear by rank-many smaller interchanges via a triangular factorization, run the bit network on row-split role streams, recurse on power widths, then pad to arbitrary widths

motivation.text: An edge matrix of rank a costs a smaller interchanges, and the ranks sum to less than W m, so the recursion saves a power of the width.

quote.quote: Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times $m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix of rank $a$ factors as $E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1,E_2$ invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ a partial permutation with $a$ ones.

quote.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

children.claim: The address shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ with $A$ of rank $a$ takes exactly $a$ smaller field interchanges plus $O(V)$ work.

quote.quote: can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit fields and $O(V)$ further work.

children.claim: The bit network with projection frames gives the shear $H\gets H+D$ on every role, with endpoint matrices differing by $I_m$ and edge ranks summing to $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$.

quote.quote: Proposition~\ref{prop:bit-motif-interface} supplies these conditions with $W=W_{\rm b}$ and $s=s_{\rm b}$.

children.claim: For widths $e=m^k$ with enough rows, the normalized cost satisfies $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, hence the interchange costs $O(Ve^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

children.claim: Supplying rows from high digits, decomposing the width in base $m$ and padding binary chunks to radix $q$ extends the bound to $O(Vu^\tau)$ for every width $u$.

quote.quote: Since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

children.salient: The final effect is an exact permutation of data, yet it is computed via XOR combinations of data and works for arbitrary scratch contents.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number of address bits in each of the two interchanged fields.

children.claim: Applying $H_0$ at one common bit position in each of $D\le d$ equal-width address chunks of polynomial records costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ with $\lambda'<1$, with exact dyadic intermediates and one final truncation.
children.method: recurse through the complex network's phase frames, realizing binary basis changes by packed address moves and converting the C-layer to the H_0 layer by phases

motivation.text: Separate butterfly factors would need one full pass per selected axis; the phase-frame recursion shares the work across axes and saves a power of d.

quote.quote: We will obtain cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with $\lambda'<1$ and $V$ the logical bit volume, whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

children.claim: With phase frames $\mathcal C_U$, each edge's frame change is a product of one two-point kernel $aI+bX_v$ per orthonormal residual vector, and telescoping gives $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role by $s_{\rm c}$ child calls on $e/m$ axes.

quote.quote: Proposition~\ref{prop:complex-motif-interface} therefore gives $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role, including roles whose initial scratch values were arbitrary.

children.salient: The same kernel tensor power appears on every role, including scratch roles.

children.claim: Diagonal phases and the scalar $b^D$ convert the exact $C^{\otimes D}$ layer into $H_0^{\otimes D}$ using only Gaussian dyadic operations.

quote.quote: Thus, once the physical binary basis changes and recursive stream layout are supplied, the complete parallel butterfly layer is exact up to its prescribed final truncation.

children.claim: Packed changes of selected address bits and the recursion give total time $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ on fixed tapes.

quote.quote: The row construction and the recurrence analysis above give total time $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ on fixed tapes, including all padded and auxiliary streams.

children.claim: Since $H_0^{\otimes D}$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, the final truncation $Q_p$ keeps values in the disk with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote: Thus $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, and componentwise truncation preserves that disk and has error less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$

adds.name: axis bound
adds.meaning: The maximum number of address chunks whose selected bits one layer acts on.

adds.name: precision
adds.meaning: The number of fractional bits of the fixed-point grid.

adds.name: logical volume
adds.meaning: The number of stored data bits of the array being processed.

children.claim: Cyclic convolution on distinct prime axes is computed from synthetic transforms over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, Gaussian resampling with retained permutations, and Bluestein chirps.
children.method: evaluate the needed transforms as synthetic polynomial transforms on a layout where the fast layers apply, and connect them to the prime-length transforms by resampling and chirps

motivation.text: In the polynomial-ring representation every transform step is an address rearrangement, a signed shift or a two-point butterfly, exactly the operations the two tape procedures accelerate.

quote.quote: In this representation, the transform calculation consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations.

children.claim: Synthetic transforms over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ on $d-1$ power-of-two axes, with outputs kept in a stored frequency order, cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$ with error below $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$.
children.method: compute Nussbaumer's decimation-in-frequency recursion, group each round into a parallel butterfly plus a monomial, and lay the selected bits out in common-offset chunks for the simultaneous layer

motivation.text: The simultaneous layer applies only to selected bits at a common offset in consecutive K-bit chunks, so a layout must be built and its movement charged.

quote.quote: To apply Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} in a transform round, we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

children.claim: With root $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$, decimation-in-frequency butterflies and signed shifts compute $B_tF_t^-$, writing the outputs directly in bit-reversed frequency order.

quote.quote: The recursion writes its outputs directly in this order; it does not move whole frequency indices.

children.claim: Each round on several axes is a parallel butterfly $\mathcal H$ followed by one recordwise monomial $J_E$.

quote.quote: Consequently the individual axis steps may be grouped as a parallel butterfly $\mathcal H$, followed by one recordwise monomial operation $J_E$.

children.claim: Moving prefix slots and interchanging chunks into the layout, and applying one simultaneous layer per round, gives the stated cost including layout construction and restoration.

quote.quote: Both layout construction and final restoration are charged in this bound.

adds.name: record length
adds.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record, a power of two.

adds.name: padded box size
adds.meaning: The number of complex entries in the padded transform array.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The width in bits of the address chunks used by the simultaneous layer.

children.claim: The normalized cyclic convolution $\mathcal M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/T$ of arrays over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ is computed with error below $\sqrt2M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$, adding only $O(Tp\log(rp))$ to the transform cost.
children.method: transform both operands forward, keep their common stored order, multiply records by signed packing, and apply the opposite transform to that order

motivation.text: The opposite transform consumes the stored order directly, so the bit-reversal and layout permutations never have to be undone between the transforms and the pointwise product.

quote.quote: We also specify where each frequency entry is stored, because the opposite transform consumes that same order after a pointwise product.

children.claim: Two polynomial records are multiplied by packing signed coefficients into integers, multiplying with the $O(n\log n)$ multiplier and unpacking, returning $Q_p(fg/r)$ in $O(rp\log(rp))$ time.

quote.quote: One can compute the exact Gaussian integer numerators of $fg$, and then return $Q_p(fg/r)$ in that same format, in time $O(rp\log(rp))$ on a fixed number of tapes.

children.claim: Both forward transforms retain their common $LB$ order, the packed products keep it, and the opposite procedure consumes it.

quote.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order.

children.claim: The tensor of prime-length source transforms satisfies $RF_{\boldsymbol s}=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ with power-of-two lengths $t_i$, contractions $\mathcal A,\mathcal B_0$, and the permutations $R,Q$ kept in the formula.
children.method: apply Harvey and van der Hoeven's one-dimensional resampling identity with both coordinate permutations retained, then take tensor products line by line using chunk swaps

motivation.text: The needed transform lengths are pairwise coprime while synthetic transforms need powers of two; resampling connects the shapes, and keeping the permutations in the formula avoids two full sorts per coordinate.

quote.quote: Its usual implementation sorts twice on each coordinate. We retain both permutations in the transform formula and compute that formula directly.

children.claim: For coprime $s<t$, $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$ with contractions $A,B_0$ computable with error below $p^2$.

quote.quote: There are linear contractions $A:\mathbb C^s\to\mathbb C^t$ and $B_0:\mathbb C^t\to\mathbb C^s$ satisfying

children.claim: Linewise tensoring gives the multidimensional identity with contractions $\mathcal A,\mathcal B_0$, and exposing lines costs $O(Tp\,d^2(1+\ell^\tau))$.

quote.quote: Both $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B_0$ are contractions.

children.claim: The middle factor $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u$ equals $\overline a\cdot(a*(\overline a\cdot u))/T$ for a chirp $a$, so it is a normalized cyclic convolution between two phase multiplications.

quote.quote: The factor $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ in \eqref{eq:no-sort-tensor} can be computed from a cyclic convolution and two pointwise phase multiplications.

children.salient: The target permutation $Q$ is absorbed into the chirp and never executed.

children.claim: The retained source permutation $R$ cancels: $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+)[(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)]=(u*v)/S^2$.

quote.quote: The second identity shows how the retained source permutation $R$ cancels when computing a convolution.

children.salient: The permutation is never undone; it cancels between the two forward transforms and the opposite one.

children.claim: The machine computes the exact $2n$-bit product of $n$-bit inputs in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time.
children.method: place the radix-digit coefficients on prime axes, reduce to ring convolution by a twist, run the transforms, recover exact coefficients, and sum the normalized cost table under fixed parameters

motivation.text: The known normalizations and an error strictly below 1/2 make rounding exact, and a compatible fixed choice of exponents puts every row of the cost table below the target power of p = Θ(log n).

quote.quote: We choose compatible parameters for these procedures, recover the integer coefficients from their approximations, and account for the remaining tape operations.

children.claim: A Chinese-remainder map $x\mapsto\prod_ix_i^{\mu_i}$ preserves cyclic convolution and is implemented by triangular controlled shifts and axis moves.

quote.quote: Hence $\Phi$ is an isomorphism and preserves cyclic convolution.

children.claim: The twist $x_d\mapsto\zeta y$ with $\zeta=e^{\pi i/r}$ turns cyclic convolution in the last coordinate into negacyclic arithmetic in $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$.

quote.quote: Untwisting therefore recovers the cyclic coefficient with the correct sign.

children.salient: The negative wrap of $y^r=-1$ reproduces exactly the positive cyclic wrap once the twist is removed.

children.claim: Splitting each input into radix-$2^b$ digits turns the product into a convolution of short coefficient lists, scaled into the disk and padded to $S$ records.

quote.quote: This produces the radix-$2^b$ digits $a_0,\ldots,a_{q-1}$ in increasing coefficient order.

children.claim: After removing the scales $S$ and $2^{2b+4}S$, the coefficient error is below $1/2$, so rounding gives the exact integers, and carry propagation yields the $2n$-bit product.

quote.quote: The strict error below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to that value the unique correct coefficient.

children.salient: Although every transform is computed only approximately, the result is exact.

children.claim: With $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}$, $\epsilon=2^{-75}$, every normalized cost in the table is at most $p^{1-2\kappa}$, so the total time is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$.

quote.quote: Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

children.salient: The binding margin is $g_2=\epsilon c(1-\tau)=2^{-181}$, from the chunk exchanges of the transform layout.

adds.name: digit width
adds.meaning: The number of bits $\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ in each radix digit.

adds.name: source box size
adds.meaning: The product of the distinct prime source axis lengths.

root.salient: The bound beats $n\log n$ by a power $(\lg n)^{\kappa}$ of the logarithm, refuting the conjectured optimality, though $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is minute.

adds.name: interchange exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-50}$ below one in the address-interchange cost.

adds.name: layer exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-54}$ below one in the butterfly-layer cost.
